A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sortformer research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and extensive restructuring.

before.justification: v2 Section V and Tables I-II report original Sortformer diarization and multi-speaker ASR experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds LibriSpeechMix results in Table 3 and runtime measurements in Section 5.4.3.

M1.justification: The core encoder, Sort Loss, hybrid loss, speaker kernels and adapters remain unchanged. v3 adds a limited adaptation using SOT-style serialized targets for LibriSpeechMix experiments, beyond v2's word-level and segment-level SST targets.

E1.justification: v3 adds LibriSpeechMix ASR training and evaluation on one-, two- and three-speaker mixtures, substantially extending coverage to heavily overlapping synthetic speech. v2 used LibriSpeech as a diarization simulation source, without this ASR benchmark. Existing diarization and real-recording ASR coverage remains.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 introduces reported comparisons against SOT-ASR, SOT-ASR-SQR, DOM-SOT and MT-LLM, substantially expanding external ASR comparisons. Table 1 also removes EEND-GLA-Small from v2 Table I while retaining EEND-GLA-Large and the other diarization comparators.

E3.justification: The new LibriSpeechMix protocol uses 2M mixtures, benchmark-specific Sortformer fine-tuning and 180K ASR updates with the diarizer frozen. Appendix D specifies ORC-WER for single-speaker baselines and cpWER for multi-speaker systems; Table 3 flags DOM-SOT's different mixture timing. Runtime testing adds a batch-size-100 protocol.

E4.justification: v3 retains the tabulated loss and real-recording ASR ablations, adds a supervision-versus-no-supervision control on LibriSpeechMix, and reports training/inference overhead analyses. v2's qualitative analysis of speaker overcounting on long recordings is omitted.

E5.justification: v3 Section 5.4.3 newly specifies 10-run averages for runtime benchmarking. v2 reports no corresponding repeated-run information. Neither version provides accuracy confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All retained diarization scores and all Table II/2 accuracy values are unchanged; EEND-GLA-Small's results are removed. New Table 3 reports Sortformer-MS-Canary scores of 2.26/4.61/9.05 for 1mix/2mix/3mix versus MS-Canary's 2.74/6.55/12.14. New runtime results report 297.891 versus 300.213 seconds without/with Sortformer.

T1.justification: v3 removes v2 Appendix B's invalid proof that self-attention is permutation invariant and revises the main-text statement to permutation equivariance. Appendices E-F add an explicit permutation-matrix definition, replace v2's erroneous equivariance identity with F(PX)=PF(X), and revise the attention derivation.

C1.justification: The core Sort Loss and differentiable ASR-integration claims persist. v3 explicitly broadens the annotation claim to eliminating segment-level timestamps, although Appendices A/C still use segment boundaries. Its conclusion also places streaming and target-speaker capabilities in future work, narrowing v2's claimed buffering and querying/targeting advantages.

C2.justification: v3 removes v2's discussion of the 90-second training versus 12-minute evaluation mismatch and associated speaker-overcount limitation. It also drops regularization, disruptive-kernel and gradient-based explanations for existing results, while adding interpretations of LibriSpeechMix performance and runtime overhead. The account of mechanisms and applicability changes substantially.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents total model sizes, timing measurements, Optuna postprocessing tuning, scoring procedures and the LibriSpeechMix training recipe. It states that code/models are available and supplies a checkpoint link, replacing v2's release promise. Conversely, detailed adapter/tokenizer descriptions and the 80-ms frontend explanation are removed.

R1.justification: v3 substantially prunes coverage of lexical diarization, streaming diarization and explicit WEEND/modular-ASR comparisons, while adding MT-LLM, MeetEval and Optuna references. The computational-graph integration novelty claim remains. Publication updates to retained works, such as NEST, do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Data cleaning, postprocessing and timestamp approximation move into Appendices A-C; a metric appendix and Impact Statement are added, and the Author Contributions section is removed.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICML formatting and single-column appendices, adds Table 3 and parameter-count columns to existing tables, and removes v2 Figures 3 and 5. The transcription comparison is redrawn as Figure 5 with an additional SOT representation, while the timestamp-approximation diagram moves to Appendix C.

improvement.justification: v2 supported ASR primarily through internal ablations; v3 adds external benchmark comparisons, a matched supervision control and runtime evidence. Removing the invalid attention-invariance proof and correcting equivariance substantially improve rigor. These gains outweigh the loss of the long-recording limitation and some implementation details, although the broader timestamp-free claim remains insufficiently qualified.
